findings.title: totalPages overcounts when the member count is an exact multiple of the page size
findings.body: `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`, so a group with exactly 50 members and limit 50 reports 2 pages. `showingLast` therefore remains false on the only real page, and the next action sets offset to `user_count`, loading an empty page. The admin UI then shows an empty final page such as `2/2` instead of disabling next. The page count should be based on `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the zero case handled), and/or the next offset should be clamped to the last valid page start.

findings.title: Public group members page only loads the first 50 members with no pagination controls
findings.body: The route now calls `model.findMembers()` once and the group model always requests the first page with `limit: 50`. The public template `group/members.hbs` renders only the returned `members` array and has no next/previous controls or infinite loading. Previously non-automatic groups returned all members. As a result, any group with more than 50 members now hides members 51+ from non-admin users with no way to reach them.

findings.title: Remove-member control is rendered for automatic groups
findings.body: This template is rendered with each `member` (a `Discourse.User`) as its context, but the guard is `{{#unless automatic}}`. `automatic` is looked up on the user, not on the parent group, so it is undefined and the remove link is rendered even for automatic groups. The server rejects the DELETE with a 422 for automatic groups, and the client has no error handling after the AJAX rejection. The group-level `automatic` flag needs to be passed into the item view or checked through the parent controller.

findings.title: Public members endpoint response shape changed from an array to an object
findings.body: `GET /groups/:group_id/members(.json)` previously returned a bare JSON array of users. It now returns `{ members: [...], meta: {...} }`. This is a breaking API change for any existing client, plugin, or integration that consumes this endpoint directly. The in-repo Ember model was updated, but there is no compatibility path or documentation for external consumers, so consumers parsing an array will start failing.

findings.title: Automatic-group remove test uses PUT although the route is DELETE
findings.body: The test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the new route is defined only as `delete "members"` and the front end sends DELETE. Controller specs bypass routing, so this test would still pass if the DELETE route were missing or wired incorrectly. It should use `xhr :delete, :remove_member` so it matches the actual contract.
